selected.upstream: XSTest v2 (Roettger et al., NAACL 2024, arXiv:2308.01263)
selected.why_selected: THE instrument named by BLANKET_REFUSER_DISQUALIFICATION. Also the only corpus here that ships per-item HUMAN refusal annotations for all five reference models, which reproduce every cell of the paper...

selected.upstream: OR-Bench (Cui et al., ICML 2025, arXiv:2405.20947), hard-1k subset
selected.why_selected: Second, independent over-refusal instrument, and the hard subset is the one that separates models: seemingly-toxic but actually-safe prompts. A single over-refusal instrument would make the disqualifi...

selected.upstream: WildGuard (Han et al., NeurIPS D&B 2024, arXiv:2406.18495)
selected.why_selected: Instrument match: WildGuard is the grader behind the ONLY non-circular external safety rows this artifact has (the Qwen3-4B-SafeRL card's 'Safety Rate (WildGuard)' and 'Refusal (WildGuard)'). Measurin...

selected.upstream: HarmBench (Mazeika et al., ICML 2024, arXiv:2402.04249), DirectRequest
selected.why_selected: The canonical harm-refusal behaviour set, with functional and semantic category labels for per-category breakdowns. Pinned via the ungated swiss-ai mirror because walledai/HarmBench is gated.

selected.upstream: AdvBench harmful behaviors (Zou et al., arXiv:2307.15043)
selected.why_selected: The most-reused harmful-behaviour set in the jailbreak literature, so an in-house number on it is the most comparable to published work. Ships the affirmative 'target' string, which is what prefix-att...

selected.upstream: JailbreakBench (Chao et al., NeurIPS D&B 2024, arXiv:2404.01318)
selected.why_selected: The only corpus here with 100 harmful behaviours and 100 deliberately MATCHED benign ones, which is exactly the paired design the blanket-refuser rule needs: the same model, the same topics, both side...

selected.upstream: Do-Not-Answer (Wang et al., EACL Findings 2024, arXiv:2308.13387)
selected.why_selected: A risk taxonomy (5 areas / 12 harm types) rather than a flat list, so refusal can be broken down by harm type. Also ships six reference models' responses with harmfulness and action labels, which is a...

selected.upstream: BeaverTails (Ji et al., NeurIPS D&B 2023, arXiv:2307.04657)
selected.why_selected: 700 prompts balanced over 14 harm categories -- the most category-balanced harm set here, which matters because refusal rates are strongly category-dependent and an unbalanced set silently measures to...

selected.upstream: ToxiGen (Hartvigsen et al., ACL 2022, arXiv:2203.09509), annotated split
selected.why_selected: Instrument match: google/gemma-2-2b-it has a PUBLISHED ToxiGen number in this artifact (48.32). ToxiGen is therefore the one corpus where an in-house measurement can be checked against an external row...

selected.upstream: NVIDIA Aegis AI Content Safety (Ghosh et al., arXiv:2404.05993)
selected.why_selected: Small (359) but carries THREE independent annotator labels per prompt, so it supplies annotator-disagreement structure the other corpora do not. Kept over the 33k-row Aegis-2.0 training set, which is ...

rejected.why_rejected: 99k web sentence PREFIXES for open-ended continuation, not instructions. The artifact measures refusal to an instruction; a truncated news sentence cannot be refused. Also 69 MB, the single largest pi...
